2. Three suits are disposed of together by the trial Court is Title Suit No.75 of 1996 was being filed by Nazrul Islam (herein called as plaintiffs) for declaration and partition. On the other hand, in Title Suit No.76 of 1996 filed by Bazlur Rahman Chawdhury herein this case called as defendant against Nazrul Islam and others for declaration that the Hiba-bil-ewaz deed dated 01.02.1984 is void, forged, collusive, operative and not binding upon the defendant. Title Suit No.78 of 1996 was filed by the defendant for recovery of khas possession over 5 square feet as described in the 3rd schedule of the plaint. All these three suits were tried analogously. 

 5. Defendant No.1 of Title Suit No.75 of 1996 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.76 of 1996 for declaration that the Hiba-bil-Ewaz deed dated 01.02.1984 executed by Rowshan Ali in favour of plaintiff No.1 of Title Suit No.75 of 1996 was void, fraudulent, inoperative and by the said deed, he had no acquired any title in the land described in the schedule to the deed. Plaintiff No.1 of Title Suit No.75 of 1996 contested Title Suit No.76 of 1996 as defendant No.1 contending that the impugned deed was genuine one. In the written statement, he narrated the story of the plaint case of Title Suit No.75 of 1996 and prayed for dismissal of this suit. He also prayed for recovery of khas possession in Title Suit No.78 of 1996 in respect of third scheduled land. 

 .02¾  ± .04¼ = .07 acre land, for which, they were entitled to get decree for partition. He further submits that the High Court Division manifestly erred in law resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice in misreading the evidence on record and failed to consider the legal and admitted facts and in basing decision on mere surmise and conjecture, since the trial Court comparing the signature of Md. Rowshan Ali as appears in the disputed solenama found that the signature of Md. Rowshan Ali does not tally with other admitted signatures of Md. Rowshan Ali and accordingly having decreed Title Suit No.75 of 1996, the appellate Court without comparing with the signature committed error in allowing the appeal, considering the certified copies of the applicants and Haziras filed by Md. Rowshan Ali in Title Suit No.75 of 1996 and holding that if the solenama, Haziras and the applications filed in the said case are genuine, the solenama cannot be a forged one without comparing the signature of Md. Rowshan Ali. He further submits that the High Court Division has misread, misconstrued and misunderstood the materials on record and consequently failed to comprehend the facts of the case and misapplied the law, since the written statement of Bazlur Rahman in Title Suit No.75 of 1996 to the effect that he got constructed of the wall in between the boundary of the land of the plaintiff and the defendant having some partition out of 1½ decimals land, he got by disputed compromise, it demonstrates that the said compromise was not acted upon and the appellate Court committed error in allowing the appeal without considering this aspect of the case. He further submits that the High Court Division failed to appreciate the facts and circumstances of the case in its true perspective, as a result of which, there has been serious miscarriage of justice, since after making the gift by Md. Rowshan Ali had no locus standi or authority to compromise the pre-emption case and the trial Court having considered this aspect of the case, rightly decreed the suit, but the appellate Court illegally held that the said gift dated 01.02.1984 has not been acted upon. He further submits that the High Court Division overlooked that the appellate Court committed error of law in allowing the appeal without considering that the defendant admitted that he got .01½ acre land by solenama and by amicable partition out of .0575 acre land and the plain-tiff got the rest of the suit land and is in possession of the same by constructing dwelling house thereon and Title Suit No.76 of 1996 filed by the defendant, Bazlur Rahman Chowdhury for recovery of khas possession also provided that the solenama was not acted upon. He further submits that the High Court Division filed to consider that the appellate Court committed error of law in holding that Md. Rowshan Ali executed the solenama and relinquished his right, title and interest over Suit Plot No. 1268 without considering that Miscellaneous Pre-emption Case No.82 of 1985 was filed by the petitioner as a 2nd class co-sharer against another 2nd class co-sharer, long after the period of limitation without making party to the present plaintiff who got the suit land by way of gift long before filing of the said pre-emption case. He finally submits that the High Court Division failed to reflect that the appellate Court committed error of law occasioning failure of justice in finding that the plaintiff could not prove his possession without discussing of the evidence and materials on record, particularly, the plaintiffs' possession in the suit land. 

 22. The High Court Division over looked that the appellate Court committed error of law in allowing the appeal without considering that the defendant admitted that the he got .011/2 acre land by solenama and by amicable partition out of .0575 acre' land and the plaintiff got the rest of the suit land and is in possession of the same by constructing dwelling house thereon and Title suit No.78 of 1996 was filed by defendant, Bazlur Rahman Chowdhury for recovery of khas possession also proved that the solenama was not acted upon. The learned Judge of the High Court Division committed a grave error of law occasioning failure of justice in not finding that the trial Court, on consideration of the evidence and materials on record, having decreed the suit in Title Suit No.75 of 1996 and dismissed Title Suit No.76 of 1996 and Title Suit No.78 of 1996. The learned appellate Court committed error in law in allowing the appeal without reversing all the findings of the trial Court.
